{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings — hosting agreement Base Terms 

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Base Terms against the playbook and confirmed 18 findings: 2 critical deviations, 4 high-severity deviations (with 2 high-severity items compliant), 5 medium-severity deviations or gaps, 1 low-severity gap, 3 medium-severity compliant items, and 2 items recorded as needs_review for internal confirmation only.

The commercial core of the risk is concentrated in four places. First, indemnity: IBM's IP indemnity in § 8.1 sits acceptably at our fallback, but § 8.2(a)(3) requires **us** to indemnify IBM for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services," leaving us exposed for IBM's own ordinary negligence and service defects — walk-away territory. Second, liability: the § 9 cap is mutual and adequately sized, but the only carve-outs are indemnification payments and bodily injury/tangible property; confidentiality and data breaches are affirmatively capped because § 6 makes §§ 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement. Third, exit economics: both § 3.4(b) (termination for convenience) and § 3.2 (renewal) are open-ended — uncapped early termination charges set in Attachment A, which IBM may unilaterally change on 90 days' notice under § 13.1, and auto-renewal for a term equal to the prior term with a 90-day notice window. Fourth, the deliverable and assurance package: Materials default to vendor-owned Type II with a narrow licence back, § 5.4(c) delivers all Materials "AS IS" with no warranty remedy anywhere, there is no transition assistance or Content return obligation, and there is no insurance clause at all.

On the positive side, we confirmed no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum purchase commitment, no non-solicitation binding us, and no audit right against us; governing law is New York (our preferred position) with no arbitration or foreign venue. Our convenience-termination notice (one month) and IBM's lack of any convenience right are better than our fallback and should be preserved.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | § 8.1 sits at our fallback (IP-only, capped credit) and is not redlined; § 8.2(a)(3) forces a one-way Customer indemnity for claims related directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services, with § 8.2(c) relief only for IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Cap basis, mutuality and the § 10 consequential-damages exclusion meet or exceed fallback; carve-outs are limited to indemnification payments and bodily injury/tangible property, with no carve-out for confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers | § 7.0 defaults all Materials to Type II (vendor-owned); the licence back is enterprise-use only with no modification or sublicensing right, and Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components is never confirmed. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License | Grant is expressly "revocable" with no standard for revocation (walk-away), and runs to Customer alone — Affiliates and our contractors are excluded, reinforced by § 14.17. Successor transfer is covered by § 14.10. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | § 3.4(b) early termination charges are set in Attachment A with no cap and no "sole remedy" language; § 13.1 lets IBM change Attachment A on 90 days' notice. § 3.3 helpfully disapplies the charges where IBM is in breach. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment | Restriction is one-directional: IBM may assign freely, including to a competitor, with no notice or consent. Our M&A successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard exist; no affiliate carve-out for us and no restriction on IBM. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity, sole-source or all-requirements obligation; § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. Preferred position met. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on us; § 14.11 No Resale and the § 12.1/§ 14.17 licence-scope limits are ordinary boundaries, and § 14.19 limits only IBM's delivery obligations. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal | Auto-renews for a term equal to the previous term (multi-year renewals — walk-away) with a 90-day non-renewal notice, above the 60-day fallback ceiling; no renewal reminder and no uplift cap. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | One month's notice for us and no IBM convenience right are better than fallback and preserved; exit cost fails the fallback — uncapped early termination charges under § 3.4(b) and no refund of prepaid Charges in § 3.5. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Reasonable care and skill plus compliance with laws, but no Deliverable/Materials conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy; § 5.4(c) delivers all Materials, including Type I, "AS IS." |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | § 3.5 addresses only payment; no exit assistance, data return, export or deletion obligation anywhere. § 14.18 covers contact information only; § 11.6 makes us responsible for Content with no return mechanic. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York substantive law (preferred); no arbitration and no foreign or vendor-home venue. Absence of an express exclusive-venue designation is noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No pricing-parity, best-price or matching obligation on us; § 14.16 confirms freedom of action. Preferred position met. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall charge; § 11.5 leaves capacity changes to our determination and § 3.4 gives an unconditional monthly exit. Attachment A and Order Forms remain to be checked. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No audit, inspection or verification right binds us — better than preferred. § 11.3 is a breach-investigation and remedy provision with no access to our premises, systems or records. Deterministic "audit frequency" check failed as an artifact of absence; no redline proposed. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | § 14.8 Personnel | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction on us — stronger than the mutual 12-month fallback. § 14.8 covers only each party's own personnel and subcontracting. Duration and carve-out checks are non-probative with no clause present; no redline proposed. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance clause anywhere; § 14.12 and § 5.3 address risk allocation and security features only. IBM operates the hosting environment and holds Customer Components, so the absence sits in walk-away territory. |

## Walk-away items

These are the findings the playbook classifies at or approaching walk-away. We would not sign without movement here.

1. **Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services — § 8.2(a)(3).** A one-way indemnity for any Services Recipient claim related directly or indirectly to the Services, with § 8.2(c) relief only where IBM's bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach caused the damages.
2. **Revocable licence — § 12.1.** The Base Components licence is expressly revocable with no standard, so IBM may withdraw it at discretion.
3. **Multi-year auto-renewal — § 3.2.** Renewal for a term equal in duration to the previous term, so a multi-year initial term auto-renews for multiple years, with a 90-day notice window.
4. **No vendor insurance.** No insurance obligation of any kind for a provider operating our hosting environment and holding Customer Components.
5. **Warranty package — § 5.1 with § 5.4(c).** No Deliverable conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy, with all Materials delivered "AS IS"; this approaches the walk-away position.

We also flag the two **critical** items as gating for signature even where not formally walk-away: the § 9 cap has no carve-out for confidentiality or data protection, and § 6 expressly makes §§ 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement for information in the hosting environment.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the deviating and missing items, in this priority order:
   - § 8.2(a)(3) — narrow our indemnity to Content and our breach of applicable law, excluding claims arising from IBM's performance.
   - New § 9.3 — add mutual uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), without reopening the cap itself.
   - § 3.4(b) / § 3.5 — cap early termination charges at three months' recurring Charges, state them as the sole amount payable and IBM's sole remedy, and add a pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges (single consolidated ask covering both the LD and T4C findings).
   - § 3.2 — 12-month renewal terms, 30-day exit notice, 60-day reminder and CPI/3% uplift cap; offer 60 days with a 5% cap as fallback.
   - § 7.0 / § 5.4 — default Materials to Customer-owned Type I, broaden the Type II licence back to include modification and sublicensing, and confirm our ownership of Content and Customer Components.
   - § 12.1 — extend the licence to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and remove at-will revocability; offer Affiliates-on-written-notice as fallback.
   - § 5.1 / § 5.4(c) — add a 90-day conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials with a no-malicious-code assurance and an at-IBM's-option re-perform/repair/refund remedy, plus an "except as expressly warranted" carve-out.
   - § 3.5 — insert post-termination transition assistance and Content return/deletion (already carried by the § 14.2 survival list).
   - § 14.10 — add an affiliate carve-out for us and mirror the consent restriction on IBM, never to a Customer competitor.
   - New § 14.12A — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
2. **Obtain and review Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms.** These are not part of the text reviewed and drive the early termination charge formula, any committed spend or minimum volume, the § 4.2 late payment fees and the § 3.5 non-terminated-attachment charges. The § 13.1 unilateral change right over Attachment A should be raised alongside the termination-charge cap.
3. **Close out the two needs_review items internally.** AUDIT and NOSOLICIT are recorded as compliant on the substance — the failed checks presuppose a clause that does not exist, and inserting limits would manufacture a right or restriction against us. No counterparty comment is to be raised. If § 11.3 is later expanded to reach our records or systems, re-run the AUDIT rule.
4. **Preserve the favourable terms in negotiation:** the one-month convenience notice and absence of any IBM convenience right (§§ 3.3–3.4), § 3.3's disapplication of termination charges where IBM is in breach, § 14.16 Freedom of Action, New York law (§ 14.3), and the mutual cap and consequential-damages exclusion structure in §§ 9–10.
5. **Note for the record, not for redline:** the absence of an express exclusive New York venue designation (§ 14.3); the § 9.1(2) exclusion of IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data (addressed under the data rules); the § 10 carve-out for amounts for Services that would have been rendered but for our breach; and § 11.3's uncapped investigation frequency with a best-efforts notice commitment."}
